# Building a To-Do App with React — Comprehensive Learning Guide ## Course Overview This medium-difficulty course teaches you how to build a fully functional to-do application using React, with a strong emphasis on JavaScript fundamentals, state management, and component architecture. You'll progress from understanding React hooks and component lifecycle to implementing features like task persistence, filtering, editing, and deletion. **Who it's for:** - Developers with foundational JavaScript knowledge looking to level up into modern frontend frameworks - Job candidates preparing for React-focused technical interviews - Anyone wanting to understand component-based UI architecture through a practical project **Why it matters for interview prep:** To-do apps are a classic technical interview project because they test your ability to: - Manage application state effectively - Build reusable, composable components - Handle user input and form management - Persist data and manage side effects - Debug and refactor code under constraints - Communicate architectural decisions Most companies (especially startups and established tech firms) will assess these exact skills when evaluating React developers. --- ## Core Topics Covered - **React Fundamentals**: Functional components, JSX syntax, and the component tree - **Hooks & State Management**: `useState`, `useEffect`, `useContext`, and custom hooks - **Event Handling & Forms**: Input validation, controlled components, and form submission - **Component Composition**: Props drilling, prop patterns, and reusable UI components - **Array Methods & Immutability**: `map()`, `filter()`, `find()`, spread operators, and state updates - **Local Storage & Persistence**: Reading/writing to browser storage and syncing with React state - **Conditional Rendering & Styling**: Dynamic CSS classes, ternary operators, and CSS-in-JS patterns - **Debugging & Performance**: React DevTools, identifying re-render issues, and optimization patterns --- ## Learning Path Workflow ### **Phase 1: React Foundations (Days 1–3)** 1. Review React component syntax and JSX 2. Master `useState` hook for managing to-do list state 3. Render a static list of tasks; practice `.map()` to display items 4. Build your first interactive component: add a task button 5. **Tasks 1–8**: Basic rendering, state updates, list display ### **Phase 2: User Input & Forms (Days 4–6)** 6. Create a controlled input component for new task entry 7. Implement form submission and input validation 8. Handle edge cases: empty strings, special characters, duplicates 9. Build delete functionality with array filtering 10. **Tasks 9–16**: Form handling, validation, array manipulation ### **Phase 3: Advanced Features (Days 7–10)** 11. Add task editing mode with inline edit forms 12. Implement task completion status (toggle complete/incomplete) 13. Build filter buttons: "All," "Active," "Completed" 14. Add priority levels and sorting functionality 15. **Tasks 17–28**: State patterns, conditional rendering, complex filtering ### **Phase 4: Data Persistence & Effects (Days 11–13)** 16. Integrate localStorage to save tasks across browser sessions 17. Use `useEffect` to sync state with localStorage 18. Handle initial load from storage on component mount 19. Implement undo/redo functionality (optional advanced feature) 20. **Tasks 29–34**: Side effects, persistence, data synchronization ### **Phase 5: Refinement & Performance (Days 14–15)** 21. Refactor components for reusability (separate task item, input form, filter buttons) 22. Optimize re-renders with React DevTools profiler 23. Implement custom hooks for business logic (e.g., `useLocalStorage`, `useTodoFilter`) 24. Add animations and transitions for better UX 25. **Tasks 35–39**: Code organization, performance tuning, polish --- ## Key Skills You'll Build ### JavaScript Mastery - **Immutable array operations**: Creating new arrays instead of mutating state - **Functional programming patterns**: `map()`, `filter()`, `reduce()`, method chaining - **Object/array destructuring**: Extracting values cleanly in function parameters - **Spread operator usage**: Combining objects and arrays, cloning with `...` - **Template literals**: Building dynamic strings for IDs, classes, and messages ### React Component Architecture - **Component decomposition**: Breaking monolithic components into smaller, single-purpose pieces - **Props flow**: Passing data and callbacks down the component tree - **State lifting**: Centralizing state in parent components when multiple children need it - **Custom hook patterns**: Extracting reusable stateful logic into hooks ### State Management Patterns - **Derived state**: Computing filtered lists on-the-fly instead of storing duplicate data - **Event handler chains**: Managing cascading updates (delete task → re-filter list → persist) - **Batch updates**: Using functional setState to handle multiple updates atomically ### Form & Input Handling - **Controlled components**: Keeping form inputs synchronized with React state - **Validation patterns**: Real-time feedback and submission guards - **Focus management**: Using refs for programmatic focus after adding/editing tasks ### Side Effects & Lifecycle - **Dependency arrays**: Understanding when effects run and how to prevent unnecessary re-runs - **Cleanup functions**: Removing event listeners and timers - **Initialization logic**: Populating state on component mount (e.g., from localStorage) --- ## Sample Problem Types ### **Problem Type 1: State & Rendering (Tasks 1–8)** **Description:** Render a list of to-do items from state and update it when a button is clicked. **Example:** ```javascript import React, { useState } from 'react'; export default function TodoList() { const [tasks, setTasks] = useState([ { id: 1, text: 'Learn React', completed: false }, { id: 2, text: 'Build a project', completed: true }, ]); const toggleTask = (id) => { setTasks(tasks.map(task => task.id === id ? { ...task, completed: !task.completed } : task )); }; return (
